en: The Chapter on Similes, Section on the Monkey.
5. The Question on the Parts of a Tree “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘three parts of a tree should be adopted,’ which are those three parts that should be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, what is called a tree is that which bears flowers and fruit;”
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga, a follower of the spiritual life, should become one who bears the flowers of liberation and the fruits of recluseship.
This, Great King, is the first quality of the tree that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, a tree gives shade to people who approach it and enter beneath it.

In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga who is a follower of the spiritual life should welcome those persons who have approached and entered [the community], whether by means of material hospitality or by means of hospitality through the Dhamma.
This, Great King, is the second quality of a tree that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, a tree does not differentiate its shade.
In the same way, great king, a yogin practicing yoga should not make any distinction among all beings;

even toward thieves, executioners, and enemies, he should cultivate an equal measure of loving-kindness toward himself, thinking: "How may these beings be free from enmity, free from affliction, free from distress, and dwell in happiness?"
This, great king, is the third quality of the tree that should be adopted.
And this was said, great king, by the Elder Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma:
the Sage is equal in all cases.”
The fifth question on the factors of a tree.
